extracted.intended_audience: physicians, medical researchers, JAMA authors, and AMA members; also interested public and policy watchers
extracted.subtask_description: Summary and explanation of a medical journal network's new public-access policy that permits immediate public deposition of accepted manuscripts and situates the change within federal OSTP guidance and open-access practices. Useful for authors, editors, and institutions seeking to understand compliance and access implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author deposit of accepted manuscript in public repository
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy permits “authors of original research investigations to deposit their accepted manuscript in a public repository of their choosing immediately on the day that the manuscript is published by the JAMA Network.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate deposit (on day of publication) into a public repository chosen by the author; expands free accessibility to all original research articles published in all JAMA Network journals. The policy applies to all authors, regardless of whether their work was federally funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'accepted manuscript'
rubrics_metrics.description: “The ‘accepted manuscript’ is the fully peer‑reviewed version of the manuscript that has been revised in response to review and is judged acceptable for publication.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted manuscript may differ from the version of record because additional edits, refinements and enhancements will still appear in the published version; the deposited accepted manuscript should link to the JAMA Network version of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access definition and options
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access means the article is freely accessible to subscribers and nonsubscribers at the time of publication with rights of reuse and redistribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JAMA Network already offers fully open-access journals (JAMA Network Open and JAMA Health Forum) and open-access options across specialty journals; the new policy provides an additional pathway (repository deposit) to expand free accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with OSTP/federal public-access guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The White House OSTP updated U.S. policy guidance recommending that the results of taxpayer-supported research be made immediately available to the American public at no cost, and agencies must update public-access policies by end of 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JAMA's policy change is in line with federal guidance and helps authors comply with anticipated or updated government public‑access requirements (affects agencies such as NIH).

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of peer review, editorial review, and post-publication enhancements
rubrics_metrics.description: The article emphasizes not overlooking “the value of peer review, editorial review, and post-publication enhancements, particularly for those who seek to translate scientific knowledge to practice and policy.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although immediate public access is supported, the journal highlights its role in summarizing and contextualizing findings for clinicians and policymakers, and the added value of editorial processes and post-publication improvements for translation to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing policy (JAMA Network)
rubrics_metrics.description: The JAMA Network journals recently adopted a new policy on sharing the data that underlies the original investigations they publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as complementary to the public-access policy, indicating an expectation or standard that underlying data for published research be shared according to the Network policy (details not specified on this page).
